          <div id="available-models" class="category-section">
            <h3 class="category-title">Available Models</h3>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Forward Dynamics Models</h3>
          <p>Models for computing forward dynamics, including acceleration computation given forces 
          and torques, suitable for simulation and analysis of multibody systems.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Inverse Dynamics Models</h3>
          <p>Implementation of inverse dynamics computations for analyzing forces and torques 
          required to achieve desired motions in multibody systems.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Kinematics and Jacobian Models</h3>
          <p>Models for computing forward kinematics, Jacobians, and other kinematic quantities 
          for multibody systems with complex joint structures.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Constraint Handling</h3>
          <p>Models and tools for handling constraints in multibody systems, including closed-loop 
          mechanisms and systems with contact constraints.</p>

        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="https://royfeatherstone.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Roy Featherstone's Website</a></h3>
          <p>Roy Featherstone is a prominent researcher in robotics and rigid-body dynamics. His website 
          offers comprehensive tutorials on spatial (6D) vectors and provides software tools for calculating 
          robot and rigid-body dynamics. Notably, it features the spatial_v2 software library, which 
          complements his authoritative book "Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms." Pinocchio is based on the 
          algorithms described in this seminal work.</p>

          study of robot dynamics, providing in-depth algorithms and methodologies essential for understanding 
          and implementing rigid body dynamics. This book is the theoretical foundation for Pinocchio and 
          is essential reading for anyone working with multibody dynamics.</p>

<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const modelsHistoryList = document.getElementById('models-history-list');
  if (!modelsHistoryList) return;

  const MODEL_PAGES = [
    'models.html',
    'models-simulink.html',
    'models-mujoco.html',
    'models-drake.html',
    'models-pinocchio.html',
    'models-pendulum.html',
    'models-opensim.html',
    'models-myosim.html'
  ];

  function updateModelsHistory() {
    let history = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('affinedrift_models_history') || '[]');
    
    const currentPage = {
      title: document.title.replace(' - AffineDrift', '').replace('AffineDrift - ', ''),
      url: window.location.pathname.split('/').pop() || 'models-pinocchio.html'
    };

    if (MODEL_PAGES.includes(currentPage.url)) {
      history = history.filter(item => item.url !== currentPage.url);
      history.unshift(currentPage);
      history = history.slice(0, 10);
      localStorage.setItem('affinedrift_models_history', JSON.stringify(history));
    }

    if (history.length === 0) {
      modelsHistoryList.innerHTML = '<li class="history-empty">No recent models yet</li>';
      return;
    }

    modelsHistoryList.innerHTML = history.map(item => 
      `<li><a href="${item.url}">${item.title}</a></li>`
    ).join('');
  }

  updateModelsHistory();
});
</script>
